summary: A rewarding Old Town temple stop for murals, a monumental Sukhothai Buddha and the red Giant Swing outside. Shortlist it if you enjoy looking closely at religious art or want a manageable addition to a historic-centre walk; the swing is a landmark to photograph, not an operating ride.
whyGo: See nineteenth-century mural painting and the large Phra Si Sakyamuni bronze Buddha.
Combine an elaborate royal temple with the open-air Giant Swing and nearby Buddhist-supply streets.
bestFor: Travellers building an Old Town walking day
skipIf: You are already feeling temple fatigue
You want an interactive attraction or a swing experience
duration: Allow 45–75 minutes for temple and exterior photographs; longer for detailed mural viewing. Planning estimate, not a timed tour.
cost: Official tourism and government visitor pages agree on THB 100 for foreign temple visitors. Viewing the Giant Swing from the public street is free. The separate residence museum is listed at THB 200 for foreigners; reconfirm before adding it.
hours: Conflicting official listings: Tourism Authority of Thailand says daily 08:00–20:00; the government's 2026 visitor guide says 08:30–16:00. Plan the interior visit within 08:30–16:00 and verify locally.
bestTime: Morning for more comfortable walking and soft light. Do the temple before relying on an evening exterior photograph.
gettingThere: 146 Bamrung Mueang Road, Phra Nakhon. Government guidance recommends MRT Sam Yot Exit 3, approximately 750 metres on foot. A taxi can reduce the walk; traffic affects journey time.
booking: Ordinary sightseeing appears to be walk-in; no official advance-ticket requirement was located. Buy admission at the temple and check any closure notice directly.
accessibility: A continuous step-free route, accessible toilet and hall access were not verified. Ask the temple about specific mobility needs; street crossings and shoe removal may matter.
practicalTips: Cover shoulders and knees and remove shoes where required before entering halls.
Carry water, a hat and a bag for shoes; the government guide notes limited shade.
Respect worshippers and posted photography restrictions. Check the entrance yourself if someone outside claims the temple is closed.
decemberNotes: Suitable for a December Old Town morning. Keep sun protection and water even during the cooler season. No special December 2026 programme or guaranteed evening interior access was verified; worship and maintenance can affect hall access.
uncertainties: Published official opening hours conflict; exact hall closing time needs checking.
December 2026 ceremonies, restoration access, museum opening and mobility facilities remain unconfirmed.
The licensed photograph dates from 2000 and shows the earlier swing structure; it illustrates the location rather than current restoration conditions.
